full_judgment: With regard to the aforesaid observation of the appellate Court I, find on tally with the lower Court's record that the said Malekunnessa is wife of late Intaj Mollah and her legal heirs having been rightly made parties in the pre-emption application. Thus, it appears to me that the pre-emption case cannot fail on the account of non-joinder of necessary parties and therefore, the case of Sultan Ahmed and others Vs Aktaruzzaman and others reported in 10 BLD(AD) 23 as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners on the point for non-impleading of necessary parties is quite distinguishable from facts and circumstance of the present case and thus the said decision in no way help to the present Pre-emptee-petitioners. Furthermore, on careful scrutiny of the pleadings of both the parties and also "their evidences on record I, find that there is no evidence at all to prove pre-emptee-petitioners have been using the Case land as their homestead. So the grievances of the learned Advocate for the petitioner are thus found to be without any foundation.
